Q1: Hydroxylamine exhibits several known hazards, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR), environmental toxicity (ENV), oral toxicity (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN), all rated at Tier 1. It also presents inhalation hazards (IHL) at Tier 2, indicating concerns beyond GHS classifications. A data deficiency (Tier 4) exists for endocrine disruption (EDC).
Q2: This chemical does not appear on any specified Lists of Concern or Lists of Low Hazard.
Q3: Hydroxylamine is extensively characterized in scientific literature, with 18,000 references, and possesses a well-defined molecular structure. While it has some toxicological data with 11 records in the EPA ToxValDB, it has not undergone the most rigorous EPA hazard evaluations such as IRIS or PPRTV.
